prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, using designed small molecules to bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase for destruction

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize. It is the clearest case on the shortlist of a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, being turned into a defined chemical reaction: a small molecule forms a ternary complex, and the cell's own machinery does the rest. The concept (Sakamoto, Crews and Deshaies, 2001) and the later structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex mechanism (Ciulli) give a transferable design rule, and the key claims have been reproduced by many independent groups, with solved VHL and cereblon/DDB1 ternary structures. Round 1 did not weaken that case. It sharpened the question of what exactly we cite, and I think a citation built on induced proximity to an E3 ligase answers it better than a PROTAC-only wording, because it keeps the glue strand inside the stated principle without adding names beyond the cap.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection stands: the PROTAC and thalidomide/cereblon glue strands may be two discoveries, and three names cannot cover Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray as well as Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. No PROTAC drug is approved yet, so the clinical consequences are promised and not demonstrated, which is a real timing weakness next to B057. I also rely on recalled, not newly verified, clinical status. If the committee decides the glue strand cannot be honoured by wording alone, a Handa-based third name or a different configuration becomes more defensible than my trio.

responses.point: B057 is mature, game-changing enabling chemistry with demonstrated consequences and a clean two-name attribution, whereas B004 is early and its credit is crowded; Handa rather than Ciulli would be the third name for B004.
responses.response: I accept that B057 is the best-confirmed and best-attributed candidate and that the missing approved PROTAC drug is a real timing point, which is why I keep B057 as an alternative. Your argument has moved me on one thing: I now treat the glue strand as the main open attribution risk and say so in the case against. I still prefer Ciulli to Handa for this configuration, because the PROTAC concept, its proof and the ternary-complex chemistry form a self-contained, independently reproduced mechanistic line, while the cereblon glue strand needs its own argument that the cap does not allow. Where we differ is weight: I value a new design principle that other chemists have independently reproduced above the maturity of an extension of a reaction class the Academy has already recognised.

responses.point: Base editing (B058) should be paired with B057 in a two-part prize, with Liu alone credited, since deaminase chemistry is a clear new capability and the chair has taken up the Liu-only suggestion.
responses.response: Thank you for taking up the Liu-only point; I do regard it as defensible, and the deamination chemistry is distinct from the nuclease cleavage honoured in 2020. My reasons for not joining your two-part configuration are measurement and timing: the first reports date from 2016 and 2017, the off-target deamination and long-term safety data are still accruing, and the independent Nishida and Kondo cytidine deaminase route makes a Liu-only citation a judgment about priority, not a neutral reading. I would add that a two-part prize here would mean two separate decisions on credit, each narrow, while B004 asks for one. I keep B058 as an alternative and would not oppose it if it carried a clear one-sentence mechanism.

responses.point: Buchwald and Hartwig independently made C-N coupling general, so a two-person prize is clean; Kosugi is a precursor and overlap with 2010 is an extension, not a duplication.
responses.response: I accept that Buchwald and Hartwig give the cleanest attribution on the list, and I agree with you and with Zou that C-N bond formation with ligand-controlled reductive elimination from amido complexes is chemically distinct from the C-C couplings of 2010. I cannot judge the 1983 tin-amide literature as an organic chemist, so I support the chair's request that the record state what Kosugi and Migita could not do. Even if that is settled in your favour, the question for me is one of principle: a very good method that extends a recognised branch, versus a new mode of pharmacology that changes what biologists and clinicians can do. That is why B057 stays my first alternative and not my preferred configuration.

responses.point: The citation should say induced proximity to the ubiquitin system so that Handa and Ito are not erased, and you weigh the lack of an approved PROTAC drug more heavily than my opening suggested.
responses.response: I agree on the induced-proximity wording and have written it into my citation. On timing I now say more plainly than in round 1 that the absence of an approved PROTAC drug is a genuine weakness, and I do not dismiss it. Where I still differ is that clinical-stage compounds, solved ternary structures and two decades of independent replication make the chemical concept validated, even if the medicine is not yet approved. I also accept your point that wording does not fully repair credit, and I treat the Handa question as unresolved, not settled.

responses.point: Biomolecular condensates (B051) reframe cellular organisation through multivalency and phase behaviour, with broad adoption across independent labs.
responses.response: The multivalency framework is attractive physical chemistry and you were candid about its limits. My view is unchanged: quantitative in-cell measurements of composition, concentration and material properties still conflict on which assemblies are true thermodynamic phases, and some functional claims rest on overexpression or reconstitution. That is the kind of unreproduced key claim I weigh heavily, so I do not place B051 in my alternatives. If you can name which in-vivo results have been independently measured and agree, I would reconsider.

uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one induced-proximity achievement or two, and whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes the prize premature this year relative to the mature B057, and whether the committee will accept my view that validated mechanism outweighs that.
Current clinical trial outcomes for degraders, which I have not verified from the files.
What the Migita/Kosugi tin-amide work could and could not do, which I cannot judge myself and which decides whether B057 is a two-name or three-name case.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited person. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase at Umeå has no direct link to B004 or the other shortlisted achievements; I note that RNR and the ubiquitin-proteasome system are both nucleotide and protein-turnover biology I follow only as a biochemist. No change since round 1.
